name: MILU
intro: MILU 是面向印度本土知识的多任务印度语言理解基准，覆盖 11 种语言、41 个学科和八大领域，并以公开考试多选题评测模型。
org: AI4Bharat, IIT Madras, IBM Research India
build_method: 公开考试题抓取, 格式/语言/去重质检, 主题恢复与聚类, 翻译补齐, 人工复核
eval_feature: Indic语言, 多学科知识, 印度文化知识
build_method_en: Public-exam scraping, format/language/dedup QC, topic recovery and clustering, translation gap filling, manual review
eval_feature_en: Indic languages, multi-subject knowledge, India-centric cultural knowledge
intro_en: MILU is a Multi-task Indic Language Understanding benchmark for India-centric knowledge, covering 11 languages, 41 subjects, and eight domains through public-exam multiple-choice questions.

drawio_review_note: Evidence-aligned against arXiv:2411.02538v3 (revised 2025-02-04; PDF SHA-256 a862d7eb687765fd056e0d312fdc0820e821fa924af286384da253bebd10aae6; TeX-source SHA-256 ddf8f4f53997d7a8c8dd4a0f8bfa40c38446de6ede603da0e552aa1348eb08b9), the official AI4Bharat/MILU repository at 7d8e6c9102bf44ae9f9ee84cfabefb4cb8fa2e88, its last task-code change at 683a6703bc2405e62bdc997fc5178e38d11ccecc, and the Hugging Face dataset listing at 946c423e72cd2657674a7a65d739e212e9a5f876 (22 listed Parquet files last changed at be958af51e203afa6628910b07ee164695be2f5f on 2025-04-28). The bilingual diagrams are topologically identical and encode the complete paper-backed construction path: more than 1,500 public national/state/regional exams spanning more than 40 exam types and more than 150K raw questions; reading-comprehension, image, over-four-option, wrong-language, and duplicate filtering; manual sample review plus IndicLID and Unicode checks; roughly 45% usable topic labels, IndicTrans2-to-English recovery, GPT-4o-mini topic naming, NV-Embed-v2, K-means with 50 clusters, and manual consolidation into 41 subjects/eight domains; task-aware GPT-4o gap filling to at least 100 and at most 500 questions per subject-language pair; and final per-language manual verification. The release branch records 79,617 four-option test questions, including 19,915 translated items, and 8,933 validation examples sampled across all 41 subjects for few-shot demonstrations, with no declared train split. It records the released row fields question, option1-option4, target, is_translated, language, domain, and subject; 11 language configs with test and validation files; CC BY 4.0 data licensing; and an auto-gated boundary. Anonymous listing was available, but payload/data-server access returned HTTP 401, so current rows were not independently audited. The evaluation branch separates the pinned open harness from the paper's API path. The harness is lm_eval 0.4.4 with test_split=test, fewshot_split=validation, first_n sampling, the exact Question/Choices A-D/Answer prompt, option1-option4 mapped to indices 0-3, conditional target-token log-likelihood selection, and mean item accuracy. The paper's closed-model path is zero-shot structured JSON because prompt log probabilities were unavailable; its exact prompt, JSON schema, parser, failure policy, model revisions, and generation parameters are not published, and no API task exists in the pinned repository. Aggregation is kept explicit: paper table cells average eight domains within each language and the overall score is the macro mean of 11 language cells (GPT-4o 74.74), while the current harness group declares weight_by_size; reweighting those already domain-averaged paper cells by test counts gives the derived counterfactual 75.95 only; it is not an official result, not interchangeable with the paper macro, and not a reproduced harness score over item-level accuracy. The diagrams also expose initial mathematics-format defects and the v3 mathematics exclusion, the 42-versus-45 model-count drift, the pinned root README conflict between the paper/table's 79,617 test rows and stale prose saying approximately 85,000, the stale nested README's 42-subject/72% claims versus v3/current-card 41-subject/74%, and undisclosed portal URLs, dates, annotator counts/agreement, dedup method, QC sample sizes, translation prompt/model snapshot, and validation seed. Both specs passed temporary strict CLI construction and XML validation under the project-standard academic-paper profile with academic-color, horizontal layout, and orthogonal routing. The diagrams use the academic-color theme's default 11px node labels; no node carries an empty style block or an ignored top-level fontSize field. The same 29-node topology was materially reflowed from a wide strip into separate construction, release, evaluation, API, reporting, and two-row evidence bands. Desktop PNGs were rendered only under /tmp at 1309 by 1545, then inspected at original resolution and at 1200px width; the site renderer's initial 0.9 scale yields about 9.9 CSS pixels. Labels fit, the validation and API dashed branches use offset positions and explicit waypoints, bilingual topology matches, connectors do not cross nodes, and the six evidence-boundary cards remain visually separate from the executable flow. No formal drawio, SVG, PNG, architecture, registry, or commit artifact was generated. Formal publication evidence [site-a11l-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1309×1548 (English) and 1309×1548 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1307×1546 and 1307×1546. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
